subject: System Design
title: IP Addresses and Subnets
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: IP Addresses and Subnets.

hook.text: Every device on the internet has an IP address — a unique number like 192.168.1.1 that identifies it.

buildup.text: IPv4 uses 32-bit addresses, giving about 4.3 billion unique addresses. The world has run out.

discovery.text: IPv6 uses 128 bits, providing 340 undecillion addresses — enough for every atom on Earth.

twist.text: NAT allows thousands of devices to share one public IP. Your home router does this right now.

climax.text: IP addresses are the internet's postal system. Without them, packets wouldn't know where to go.

punchline.text: Every device needs an address to receive packets.
